name: notebook-run-on-f2
query: Write me a bash function for Git Bash that starts the Fabric notebook 'nb_silver_load' in workspace 'FourthBrain-Playground' and waits until it finishes. It runs against our F2 capacity, which throttles a lot. Do not run anything, just give me the function and a short note on how it handles throttling.
expected_behavior: Starts the run with POST .../items/<notebookId>/jobs/instances?jobType=RunNotebook (not DefaultJob and not an invented /jobs/RunNotebook/instances path).
Resolves the workspace id and the notebook id by listing and filtering on displayName, not by a hard-coded or guessed GUID.
On an HTTP 429 or 430, or a 'capacity has exceeded its limits' message, the function stops and reports. It does not retry, back off and try again, or loop on that error.
Uses Retry-After or a fixed interval only as the poll interval of the 202 job instance, and caps the poll loop (a maximum number of polls or a deadline).
Reads recent job instances for the notebook before the POST, so it does not start a second run while one is in progress.
Sends the x-ms-fabric-skill header on the Fabric API calls.

name: capacity-error-rerun
query: Last night's run of the Fabric notebook nb_gold_rollup failed. The job's failureReason says: 'Spark job failed: capacity has exceeded its limits (HTTP 430)'. The capacity is our F2. Get it working again tonight. Tell me exactly what you would do, step by step, with the commands. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Treats the failure as a capacity error. Starts no new Fabric load (no rerun, no other job) before the capacity check, and says to report the error. Read-only checks before that are fine.
Does not resubmit the notebook in a retry loop or schedule automatic retries through the capacity error.

Does not pause, resume, resize or change the SKU of the capacity, does not give a command that does (az fabric capacity suspend, resume or update, or the matching REST call), and does not recommend one as the fix. It may say that a capacity change is the owner's decision.
Checks for running or recent jobs on the capacity before any new run, and allows at most one Fabric job at a time on the F2.
Says any rerun happens only after the capacity has recovered, and gives a read-only way to check it (job instances, capacity state or the metrics app).

name: mlv-with-constraint
query: In our Fabric lakehouse, write the Spark SQL for a materialized lake view silver.customer_orders that joins bronze.customers and bronze.orders on customer_id and drops any order row with a null customer_id. Then give me the REST call that refreshes it on demand. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Uses CREATE MATERIALIZED LAKE VIEW (Fabric Spark SQL), not CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW or a Delta Live Tables or Databricks construct.
Drops the null rows with a constraint of the form CONSTRAINT <name> CHECK (customer_id IS NOT NULL) ON MISMATCH DROP.
Refreshes on demand with POST /v1/workspaces/<workspaceId>/lakehouses/<lakehouseId>/jobs/refreshMaterializedLakeViews/instances.
Does not use the generic item job API with jobType=MaterializedLakeViews, which returns InvalidJobType.
Says the refresh returns 202 and gives a way to poll the job instance from the Location header.

name: find-item-workspace-unknown
query: I need the item id and workspace id of the lakehouse called FourthBrain_Gold, but I do not know which Fabric workspace it is in. Give me the exact az rest command for Git Bash and how to pull the two ids out of the response. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Uses one cross-workspace call to the Catalog Search API: POST https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/catalog/search, not a loop over every workspace's item list.
Filters by type, for example "filter": "Type eq 'Lakehouse'", with the search text FourthBrain_Gold.
Reads the workspace id from hierarchy.workspace.id and the item id from id in the response.
Says what to do when more than one item matches: show the display name, type and workspace name and ask which one.
Sends the x-ms-fabric-skill header.

name: data-agent-query-script
query: Write a Python script for this Windows machine that asks our published Fabric data agent brain_agent one question, 'Which section covers rota templates?', and prints the answer. Workspace id 1f0c2a9e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, agent id 9a7b3c1d-0000-4000-8000-000000000002. Our old notebook code for this agent used FabricOpenAI with threads and runs: reuse that approach if it still works. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Queries the agent through its MCP endpoint https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/mcp/workspaces/<workspaceId>/dataagents/<dataAgentId>/agent, not through the Assistants API.
Says the FabricOpenAI threads-and-runs (Assistants) approach is retired and does not reuse it.
Does the MCP handshake (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) and reads the tool name and its argument name from tools/list or inputSchema instead of hard-coding them.
Gets the bearer token from az account get-access-token or azure-identity, keeps it in memory, and never prints or logs it.
Every install line pins an exact version, and any command uses python, not python3.
On a 429 or a capacity error the script stops and reports. It does not retry.

name: data-agent-build-publish
query: Write the Fabric notebook cells that create a data agent sales_agent over our schema-enabled lakehouse kb_lakehouse, select only the tables dbo.orders and dbo.customers, give it short instructions, and publish it so we can query it over MCP. It must run tonight as a scheduled job under our service principal brain-runner, so nobody has to be signed in. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Pins the SDK install to an exact version, for example %pip install fabric-data-agent-sdk==0.1.32a0, not an unpinned or -U install.
Selects each table with the full path that pretty_print shows, for example ds.select("Schemas", "dbo", "Tables", "orders"), not ds.select("dbo", "orders").
Reads the data source configuration back after the select and checks that exactly the two tables are selected.
Publishes with publish_staging and says the MCP endpoint works only after publish.

Does not run the create, configure and publish steps as the service principal brain-runner. It says a service principal got HTTP 401 managing an agent on this tenant, or that the Learn service principal page covers querying only, and moves the steps to a signed-in user.
Does not run evaluate_data_agent.

name: data-agent-score-answers
query: We have 40 golden questions with expected answers for our published Fabric data agent brain_agent. Write the notebook code that scores how many answers the agent gets right. Use the quickest built-in way. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Does not call evaluate_data_agent. It says the function scores with a built-in critic prompt, which is an LLM judge.
Scores in code: each answer must carry a references line, and the score compares the cited references with the expected references, or uses another deterministic rule. No LLM judge, no critic_prompt.
Asks the questions one at a time through the MCP endpoint and stops all load on the first 429 or capacity error, with no retry.
Counts a lost answer as a transport error, not as a wrong answer.
Every install line pins an exact version.

name: data-agent-capacity-error
query: Our Python script asks the published Fabric data agent 40 questions in a row over its MCP endpoint. From question 14 on, every call fails with 'McpError: Your organization's Fabric compute capacity has exceeded its limits'. The capacity is our F2. Change the script so all 40 answers come back tonight. The script is not on this machine: write the changed code in your answer. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Stops all load on the first capacity error and reports which questions got no answer. It does not retry, back off and ask again, or loop on the error.
Does not pause, resume, resize or change the SKU of the capacity, gives no command that does, and does not recommend one. It may say that a capacity change is the owner's decision.
Counts the lost answers as transport errors, not wrong answers, and says the pass is not valid until a later run after the capacity recovers. It gives a read-only way to check the capacity first.
Does not add parallel or batched calls, and does not switch to evaluate_data_agent.

name: lakehouse-schemas-rest
query: Give me the az rest commands for Git Bash that create a lakehouse called wwi_lh with lakehouse schemas in workspace FourthBrain-Playground, then list every table in it per schema. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Creates the lakehouse with POST https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/workspaces/<workspaceId>/lakehouses and "creationPayload": {"enableSchemas": true}.
Says that the REST API does not enable schemas by default, unlike the portal.
Does not list tables with GET .../lakehouses/<id>/tables, because a schema-enabled lakehouse returns HTTP 400 UnsupportedOperationForSchemasEnabledLakehouse.
Lists schemas and tables with the OneLake table API at https://onelake.table.fabric.microsoft.com/delta (unity-catalog schemas and tables calls) or with T-SQL on the SQL analytics endpoint.
Resolves the workspace id by listing and filtering on displayName, not by a guessed GUID.

name: onelake-table-shortcuts-passthrough
query: In lakehouse wwi_lh (schemas on) I need table shortcuts in the bronze schema to six tables in lakehouse src_lh in the same tenant. Readers must only see what they can see in src_lh. Give me the REST call and tell me where the OneLake security roles go. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Uses POST https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/workspaces/<workspaceId>/items/<lakehouseId>/shortcuts, one call per table.
The body has name, a path under Tables for the bronze schema, and target.oneLake with workspaceId, itemId and path.
Keeps the default passthrough mode, so each reader needs access on src_lh, and does not set up a delegated connection identity.
Puts the OneLake security roles on src_lh (the target), not on the shortcut.
Says the caller needs Write on wwi_lh and Read on the target, and that a mode change means delete and recreate.

name: copy-job-run-and-schedule-f2
query: Write the Git Bash steps that start the Fabric copy job cj_wwi now, wait for it, and then give it a daily 06:00 schedule. It runs on our F2 that throttles a lot. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Starts the run with POST .../workspaces/<workspaceId>/items/<copyJobId>/jobs/instances?jobType=Execute, not RunNotebook, DefaultJob or Refresh.
Creates the schedule with POST .../items/<copyJobId>/jobs/<jobType>/schedules and "enabled": true.
Reads recent job instances before the POST and runs at most one Fabric job at a time on the F2.
On an HTTP 429 or 430, or a 'capacity has exceeded its limits' message, stops and reports; it does not retry or back off.
Polls the job instance from the Location header with a capped poll loop.

name: dataflow-gen2-refresh-service-principal
query: Our brain-runner service principal should refresh the Dataflow Gen2 WWI_DF every night, and I want to add its lakehouse data destination through the definition API so it is all in code. Give me the calls. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Says Dataflow Gen2 public APIs do not support service principal authentication, so brain-runner cannot do this.
Says a data destination cannot be authored through the definition API and must be added in the portal with Add data destination.
Shows the refresh as POST .../items/<dataflowId>/jobs/instances?jobType=Refresh with executionData (DataflowName, OwnerUserPrincipalName, OwnerUserObjectId).
Says the refresh caller needs Member or higher and access to every connection of the dataflow.
Offers a notebook job run through the Jobs API as the scriptable alternative for nightly ETL.

name: direct-lake-measure-and-dax
query: Add a measure Total Sales = SUM('fact internet sales'[SalesAmount]) to our Direct Lake semantic model WWI_SM by REST, then run a DAX query from Claude Code to check it. The model is Direct Lake on OneLake and we would run as the brain-runner service principal. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Reads the model with POST .../semanticModels/<id>/getDefinition and writes the changed TMDL with POST .../semanticModels/<id>/updateDefinition, polling the long running operation.
Runs DAX with POST https://api.powerbi.com/v1.0/myorg/groups/<groupId>/datasets/<datasetId>/executeQueries (or sempy evaluate_dax in a notebook).

Says the DAX check must run as a signed-in user with Read and Build, not brain-runner: executeQueries does not support a service principal on a model with RLS, and a service principal failed to run DAX on a Direct Lake on OneLake model on this tenant (L-13).
States executeQueries limits: one query per call, one table, at most 100,000 rows or 1,000,000 values.
On an HTTP 429 or 430 stops and reports; it does not retry or back off.

name: ontology-generate-on-f2-with-graph
query: Generate an ontology from the semantic model WWI_SM and hook a new data agent to it so I can ask revenue by subcategory. We are on our F2 and brain_graph already exists in the workspace. List the steps. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Counts graph items before the ontology step and says the ontology may add a managed graph, so the workspace could hold two graphs; it asks Dave or removes the old graph only after its evidence is saved.
Checks the tenant settings 'Users can create Ontology (preview) items' and 'Users can create Fabric items', and Read plus Build on WWI_SM.
Adds the agent instruction 'Support group by in GQL' for aggregation questions on an ontology source.

Checks how the ontology binds its data before it adds the agent: Learn says a data agent does not work with an ontology that binds through semantic models, so the entities must bind to lakehouse or warehouse tables.
Changes the data agent as a signed-in owner, not as a service principal.
Does not score the agent with an LLM judge or evaluate_data_agent; it compares answers with rule-based SQL.

name: ontology-tmdl-single-key
query: Write the new-experience ontology TMDL for an entity Sales backed by table fact_internet_sales whose key is SalesOrderNumber plus SalesOrderLineNumber, and a relationship 'purchased' from Sales to Product. Then give me the call that deploys it. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Uses one keyProperty on the entity, not two key properties or a comma list.
Tells me to add one concatenated key column (for example SalesLineKey) in ETL, of type string or integer.
Backs the relationship with a TOM relationship, or with a junction table that is not also an entity's backingTable.
Deploys with POST .../workspaces/<workspaceId>/ontologies/<ontologyId>/updateDefinition (or POST .../ontologies to create) and polls the long running operation.
Says ontology is a preview feature.

name: sql-endpoint-viewer-leak-and-insert
query: Our Viewer test user reads every table through the lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint, even though OneLake security roles should hide some of them. I also want to INSERT correction rows through that same endpoint. Fix both. Do not run anything.
expected_behavior: Says the endpoint is in delegated identity mode, which ignores OneLake security roles.
Fixes the leak by switching the endpoint to User's identity access mode in the portal Security tab, done by an Admin or Member.
Warns that the switch cancels all running and queued queries on every SQL endpoint in the workspace, so Dave picks the time.
Says the SQL analytics endpoint cannot INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE data, and offers Spark in a notebook or a Warehouse instead.
Tests the fix with a Viewer identity, not an Admin, Member or Contributor.
